title: Program meets a relation
statement: Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be a set of execution limits, let $P$ be a program, and let $p,d,T\in\mathbb N$, $\mathrm{vals}\in\mathbb Z^{*}$, and $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Let $R$ be a predicate on pairs consisting of an integer and a memory function $\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. The program meets $R$ at position $p$ and depth parameter $d$ if there is a statement body at position $p$ in $P$ and, starting from the state with local frame initialized by $\mathrm{vals}$ and memory $\mu$, execution under limits $\mathrm{lim}$ can end after $T$ steps in a state whose location-zero value and memory satisfy $R$.
hypotheses_covered: A predicate $R$ on an integer and a memory function
There is a body at position $p$ in $P$
Execution from the specified initial state ends after $T$ steps in a state satisfying $R$
caveat: The snippet leaves the definitions of execution, the initial frame, and state locations such as $\mathrm{Ends}$, $\mathrm{frame}$, and $\mathrm{loc}$ unspecified, so their exact meaning cannot be recovered here.
